items.stem: Which of the following statements about motion in a straight line is correct?
items.answer: Instantaneous velocity is the slope of the position-time graph at that instant.
items.markingKey: (c) Correct: "Instantaneous velocity is the slope of the position-time graph at that instant." The other three are false.
options: Instantaneous speed can be different from the magnitude of instantaneous velocity.
A body moving at constant speed must have constant velocity even if it reverses direction.
Instantaneous velocity is the slope of the position-time graph at that instant.
Path length can be negative.

items.stem: A runner completes one full lap of a 400 m track. What are the path length and displacement? Explain the difference.
items.markingKey: Path length counts the whole track (1 mark); displacement is final minus initial position, which coincide (1 mark).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The magnitude of displacement can exceed the path length.
Reason (R): Displacement is the shortest distance between initial and final positions.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false; R is true and shows displacement ≤ path length.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Farhan walks 750 m due east to a market in 14 min and then 300 m due west in 9 min. Find (i) the path length, (ii) the displacement, (iii) the average speed and (iv) the average velocity, in SI units.
items.answer: (i) 1050 m (ii) 450 m east (iii) 0.761 m s⁻¹ (iv) 0.326 m s⁻¹ east
items.markingKey: Path 750 + 300 = 1050 m; displacement 750 − 300 = 450 m east; time 23 min = 1380 s; average speed 1050/1380 = 0.761 m s⁻¹; average velocity 450/1380 = 0.326 m s⁻¹ east.

items.stem:
A Kolkata Metro train runs along a straight track through stations P, Q, R and S. The gaps are PQ = 1.8 km, QR = 1.6 km and RS = 2.1 km. It takes 4 min, 4 min and 4 min for the three runs and stops for 0.5 min at Q and at R.
(i) What is the displacement from P to S? (ii) Find the average speed from P to S in km h⁻¹. (iii) Find the average speed between P and Q in m s⁻¹. (iv) If the train returns from S to P, what is its average velocity for the round trip?
items.answer: (i) 5.5 km (ii) 25.4 km h⁻¹ (iii) 7.50 m s⁻¹ (iv) zero
items.markingKey: (i) 1.8 + 1.6 + 2.1 = 5.5 km (1). (ii) time = 13 min; 5.5/(13/60) = 25.4 km h⁻¹ (1). (iii) 1800 m / 240 s = 7.50 m s⁻¹ (1). (iv) Displacement zero, so average velocity zero (1).

items.stem: The position of a particle moving along the x-axis is x = 9 + 5t + 0.5t² (x in metres, t in seconds). Find (i) its velocity at t = 6 s and (ii) its average velocity between t = 2 s and t = 6 s.
Convert a speed of 126 km h⁻¹ into m s⁻¹.
Explain why the position-time graph of a body at rest is a straight line parallel to the time axis.
items.answer: x does not change with t, so the slope (velocity) is zero.
items.markingKey: Constant x (1 mark); zero slope = zero velocity (1 mark).

items.stem: A bus covers the first half of the distance from Indore to Delhi at 72 km h⁻¹ and the second half at 40 km h⁻¹. Find its average speed for the whole journey.

Gauri walks from home to a market 3 km away at 5 km h⁻¹. Finding it closed, Gauri turns back at once and walks home at 10 km h⁻¹. Find the magnitude of average velocity and the average speed over the interval 0 to 43 min.
items.answer: Average velocity 2.56 km h⁻¹; average speed 5.81 km h⁻¹
items.markingKey: Outward time 36 min. In the remaining 7 min the return distance is 10 × 0.1167 = 1.167 km. Displacement 1.833 km, path 4.167 km in 43 min = 0.7167 h; |v_av| = 2.56 km h⁻¹, speed = 5.81 km h⁻¹.

items.stem: The position of a particle moving along the x-axis is x = 5 + 10t + t² (x in metres, t in seconds). Find (i) its velocity at t = 6 s and (ii) its average velocity between t = 4 s and t = 6 s.

Assertion (A): A car moving on a circular track at constant speed has constant velocity.
Reason (R): Velocity is a vector.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false because direction keeps changing; R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Karthik walks 450 m due east to a market in 12 min and then 400 m due west in 9 min. Find (i) the path length, (ii) the displacement, (iii) the average speed and (iv) the average velocity, in SI units.
items.answer: (i) 850 m (ii) 50 m east (iii) 0.675 m s⁻¹ (iv) 0.0397 m s⁻¹ east
items.markingKey: Path 450 + 400 = 850 m; displacement 450 − 400 = 50 m east; time 21 min = 1260 s; average speed 850/1260 = 0.675 m s⁻¹; average velocity 50/1260 = 0.0397 m s⁻¹ east.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about acceleration is NOT correct?
items.answer: For uniformly accelerated motion the position-time graph is a straight line.
items.markingKey: (b) "For uniformly accelerated motion the position-time graph is a straight line." is false; the other three are true.
options: For uniformly accelerated motion the velocity-time graph is a straight line.
For uniformly accelerated motion the position-time graph is a straight line.
A body can have zero velocity and non-zero acceleration at the same instant.
Negative acceleration does not always mean the body is slowing down.

items.stem: Why do the kinematic equations v = v₀ + at etc. not apply to a car in city traffic?
items.answer: They hold only for constant (uniform) acceleration; city traffic has continually changing acceleration.
items.markingKey: Uniform acceleration condition (1 mark); application (1 mark).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The velocity-time graph for uniformly accelerated motion is a parabola.
Reason (R): v = v₀ + at.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: v = v₀ + at is a straight line; R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A scooter moving at 8 m s⁻¹ accelerates uniformly at 3 m s⁻² for 11 s. Find its final velocity and the distance travelled in this time.
A car moving at 90 km h⁻¹ is brought to rest in 30 m by applying the brakes uniformly. Find the retardation and the time taken to stop.

Kunal is driving at 36 km h⁻¹ when a child runs onto the road. Kunal's reaction time is 0.6 s and the brakes give a retardation of 6 m s⁻². Find the total stopping distance. What would it be at 72 km h⁻¹ with the same reaction time and braking?
items.markingKey: u = 10 m s⁻¹. Reaction distance = u t_r = 6 m (1); braking distance = u²/2a = 8.33 m (1); total 14.3 m (1). Doubling u doubles the reaction distance and quadruples the braking distance: 45.3 m.

items.stem: A body starts with velocity 10 m s⁻¹ and moves with uniform acceleration 2 m s⁻². How far does it travel during the 4th second?

Yash's car waits at a traffic signal. As the light turns green, it starts with uniform acceleration 2.5 m s⁻². At that instant Aditya's car passes it at a constant 12 m s⁻¹. When and where does Yash overtake Aditya? What is Yash's speed then?
items.answer: After 9.60 s, 115 m from the signal; speed 24.0 m s⁻¹
items.markingKey: ½at² = vt ⇒ t = 2v/a = 9.60 s (1.5); distance vt = 115 m (1); speed at = 24.0 m s⁻¹ (0.5).

items.stem: Derive v = v₀ + at for uniformly accelerated motion using a velocity-time graph.
items.markingKey: Draw v-t straight line from v₀ (1); slope = acceleration a = (v − v₀)/t (2); rearrange (2).

items.stem: A uniformly accelerated body covers 16 m in the first 2 s and 32 m in the next 2 s. Find its initial velocity and acceleration.
items.answer: u = 4 m s⁻¹, a = 4 m s⁻²
items.markingKey: 16 = 2u + ½a(2)²; 48 = 4u + ½a(4)² (2 marks). Solving: a = (s₂ − s₁)/t² = 4 m s⁻², u = 4 m s⁻¹ (3 marks).

items.stem: A local train starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 1 m s⁻² for 26 s, then runs at constant speed for 81 s and finally retards uniformly at 2 m s⁻² to stop. Find the total distance covered and the average speed.
items.markingKey: Max speed 26 m s⁻¹ (1); distances 338 m + 2106 m + 169 m = 2610 m (2); time 120 s; average 21.8 m s⁻¹ (1).

items.stem: Give an example where the acceleration is negative but the body speeds up.
items.answer: A body moving in the −x direction with increasing speed, e.g. a ball falling when upward is taken as positive.
items.markingKey: Sign convention (1 mark); valid example (1 mark).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about acceleration is NOT correct?
items.answer: A body with zero velocity must have zero acceleration.
items.markingKey: (d) "A body with zero velocity must have zero acceleration." is false; the other three are true.
options: A body can have zero velocity and non-zero acceleration at the same instant.
For uniformly accelerated motion the velocity-time graph is a straight line.
Negative acceleration does not always mean the body is slowing down.
A body with zero velocity must have zero acceleration.

items.stem: Explain why the stopping distance of a vehicle becomes four times when its initial speed is doubled (same braking).
items.answer: Stopping distance = v₀²/2a ∝ v₀², so doubling v₀ gives 4 times the distance.
items.markingKey: v² = v₀² − 2ax with v = 0 (1 mark); x ∝ v₀² (1 mark).

items.stem: A car moving at 90 km h⁻¹ is brought to rest in 20 m by applying the brakes uniformly. Find the retardation and the time taken to stop.

A local train starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 0.5 m s⁻² for 21 s, then runs at constant speed for 87 s and finally retards uniformly at 3 m s⁻² to stop. Find the total distance covered and the average speed.
items.markingKey: Max speed 10.5 m s⁻¹ (1); distances 110.25 m + 913.5 m + 18.375 m = 1040 m (2); time 111.5 s; average 9.35 m s⁻¹ (1).

items.stem: Which kinematic equation should be used when the time taken is not known?
items.markingKey: (c) v² = v₀² + 2ax has no t.
options: v = v₀ + at
x = v₀t + ½at²
v² = v₀² + 2ax
x = vt

items.stem: A uniformly accelerated body covers 21 m in the first 3 s and 57 m in the next 3 s. Find its initial velocity and acceleration.
items.answer: u = 1 m s⁻¹, a = 4 m s⁻²
items.markingKey: 21 = 3u + ½a(3)²; 78 = 6u + ½a(6)² (2 marks). Solving: a = (s₂ − s₁)/t² = 4 m s⁻², u = 1 m s⁻¹ (3 marks).

items.stem: What does the area under an acceleration-time graph represent?
items.markingKey: (c) The area under an acceleration-time graph gives the change in velocity.
options: displacement
velocity
change in velocity
acceleration

items.stem: Why can a position-time graph never be a vertical line?
items.answer: A vertical line would mean infinite velocity, or the body being at many positions at one instant.
items.markingKey: Slope → ∞ (1 mark); impossible (1 mark).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A body falling freely from rest covers distances in the ratio 1 : 3 : 5 in successive equal intervals.
Reason (R): For free fall from rest, distance ∝ t².
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A stone is dropped from a bridge over the Yamuna 30 m high. Find the time taken to reach the ground and the speed on reaching it. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²; neglect air resistance)
A ball is thrown vertically upward with a speed of 24.5 m s⁻¹. Find the maximum height it reaches and the time after which it returns to the thrower's hand. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)

A ball is thrown vertically upward with a velocity of 10 m s⁻¹ from the top of a multistorey building 50 m high. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², (i) how high above the ground will it rise, and (ii) how long after being thrown will it hit the ground?
items.markingKey: (i) rise above top = u²/2g = 5 m, so 55 m above ground (1.5). (ii) take up as +: −50 = 10t − 5t² ⇒ 5t² − 10t − 50 = 0 ⇒ t = 4.32 s (rejecting the negative root) (1.5).

items.stem: The velocity-time graph of a car rises in a straight line from 0 to 10 m s⁻¹ in 3 s, stays at 10 m s⁻¹ for the next 13 s and then falls in a straight line to zero in 4 s. Find (i) the acceleration in the first part, (ii) the total distance and (iii) the average speed.

A balloon is rising vertically at a steady 12 m s⁻¹. When it is 40 m above the ground, a packet is released from it. Find the time taken by the packet to reach the ground and its speed on hitting the ground. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
items.markingKey: The packet starts with the balloon's velocity 12 m s⁻¹ upward (1). −40 = 12t − 4.9t² ⇒ t = 4.33 s (2). v² = u² + 2gh ⇒ v = 30.5 m s⁻¹ (1).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about a ball thrown vertically upward (air resistance neglected) is NOT correct?
items.answer: Its acceleration is zero at the highest point.
items.markingKey: (b) "Its acceleration is zero at the highest point." is false; the other three are true.
options: It returns to the thrower's hand with the speed it was thrown with.
Its acceleration is zero at the highest point.
Its velocity at the highest point is zero.
The time of ascent equals the time of descent.

items.stem: The velocity-time graph of a cyclist is a horizontal line at 8 m s⁻¹ from t = 0 to t = 10 s. How far does the cyclist travel?
items.markingKey: Area under the v-t graph = 8 × 10 = 80.0 m.

items.stem: What does the area under a velocity-time graph represent?
items.markingKey: (c) The area under a velocity-time graph gives the displacement.
options: acceleration
velocity
displacement
change in velocity

items.stem: A body falls freely from rest. How far does it fall during the 7th second? (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) What is the ratio of this to the distance fallen in the 1st second?
items.markingKey: s_n = (g/2)(2n − 1) = 4.9 × 13 = 63.7 m; ratio 13 : 1 (Galileo's law of odd numbers).

items.stem: Two balls are dropped from the same height at the same time, one heavy and one light. In the absence of air resistance, which reaches first? Explain.
items.markingKey: Free-fall acceleration g is the same for all bodies (1 mark); same h, same t = √(2h/g) (1 mark).

items.stem:
During a school sports day, Ananya tosses a cricket ball vertically upward with a speed of 9.8 m s⁻¹ and catches it at the same height. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻² and upward as positive.
(i) What is the velocity of the ball at the highest point? (ii) Find the maximum height. (iii) Find the total time in the air. (iv) What is the acceleration of the ball at the highest point?
The velocity-time graph of a ball thrown upward is a straight line crossing the time axis. What does the crossing point show and why is the slope negative?
items.answer: The crossing is the highest point (v = 0); slope = −g because acceleration is downward.
items.markingKey: Each point 1 mark.

items.stem: A stone is dropped from a water tank 80 m high. Find the time taken to reach the ground and the speed on reaching it. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²; neglect air resistance)

Assertion (A): In the absence of air, a feather and a coin dropped together reach the ground together.
Reason (R): The acceleration due to gravity is independent of the mass of the body.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about relative velocity in one dimension is correct?
items.markingKey: (c) Correct: "v_AB = −v_BA." The other three are false.
options: The velocity of A relative to B is v_A + v_B for bodies moving in the same direction.
Relative velocity is always greater than the velocity of either body.
v_AB = −v_BA.
Two bodies with equal velocities have relative velocity 2v.

items.stem: Why does a train coming from the opposite direction seem to pass much faster than one overtaking you?
items.answer: In opposite directions the relative speed is the sum of the speeds; in the same direction it is the difference.
items.markingKey: Each case 1 mark.

items.stem: Two cars move on a straight highway towards each other at 90 km h⁻¹ and 72 km h⁻¹. What is the magnitude of the velocity of one relative to the other?
items.markingKey: Opposite directions: v₁ + v₂ = 162 km h⁻¹.

items.stem: Two trains of lengths 250 m and 300 m run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 90 km h⁻¹ and 54 km h⁻¹. How long do they take to cross each other?
items.markingKey: Relative speed = 40 m s⁻¹; distance to cover = 250 + 300 = 550 m; t = 550/40 = 13.8 s.

items.stem: A police jeep is chasing a speeding car on a straight highway. The car moves at 60 km h⁻¹ and the jeep at 90 km h⁻¹; initially the jeep is 500 m behind. How long does the jeep take to catch the car, and how far does the car travel in that time?
Show that the position-time graphs of two bodies moving with equal velocities are parallel straight lines.
items.answer: Both have the same slope, so the gap x_B − x_A stays constant.
items.markingKey: Slope = velocity (1 mark); constant separation (1 mark).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A passenger in a train moving at 60 km h⁻¹ sees a parallel train moving at 60 km h⁻¹ in the same direction as stationary.
Reason (R): Their relative velocity is zero.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Two cyclists ride along a straight road in the same direction. A moves at 22 m s⁻¹ and B at 17 m s⁻¹. What is the velocity of B relative to A?
items.markingKey: v_BA = v_B − v_A = 17 − 22 = −5.0 m s⁻¹ (falling behind).

items.stem: Two cyclists ride along a straight road in the same direction. A moves at 24 m s⁻¹ and B at 11 m s⁻¹. What is the velocity of B relative to A?
items.markingKey: v_BA = v_B − v_A = 11 − 24 = −13 m s⁻¹ (falling behind).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about relative velocity in one dimension is correct?
items.answer: The velocity of A relative to B is v_A − v_B.
items.markingKey: (a) Correct: "The velocity of A relative to B is v_A − v_B." The other three are false.
options: The velocity of A relative to B is v_A − v_B.
Two bodies with equal velocities have relative velocity 2v.
The velocity of A relative to B is v_A + v_B for bodies moving in the same direction.
v_AB = v_BA.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): v_AB = −v_BA.
Reason (R): Relative velocity depends on the frame from which it is observed.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (b) Both true, but R does not explain the sign relation.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Two cars move on a straight highway in the same direction at 60 km h⁻¹ and 90 km h⁻¹. What is the magnitude of the velocity of one relative to the other?
items.markingKey: Same direction: |v₁ − v₂| = 30.0 km h⁻¹.

items.stem: Derive v² = v₀² + 2ax using the calculus method (a = v dv/dx).
items.markingKey: a = dv/dt = v dv/dx (2); ∫v dv from v₀ to v = a ∫dx from 0 to x (2); ½(v² − v₀²) = ax (1).

items.stem: A scooter moving at 10 m s⁻¹ accelerates uniformly at 1.5 m s⁻² for 11 s. Find its final velocity and the distance travelled in this time.
A uniformly accelerated body covers 27.5 m in the first 5 s and 52.5 m in the next 5 s. Find its initial velocity and acceleration.
items.answer: u = 3 m s⁻¹, a = 1 m s⁻²
items.markingKey: 27.5 = 5u + ½a(5)²; 80 = 10u + ½a(10)² (2 marks). Solving: a = (s₂ − s₁)/t² = 1 m s⁻², u = 3 m s⁻¹ (3 marks).

items.stem: Why do we say that the speedometer of a car shows instantaneous speed and not average speed?
items.answer: It shows the speed at that instant (over a very short interval), which changes from moment to moment.
items.markingKey: Instantaneous = limit over very small Δt (1 mark); reading changes continuously (1 mark).

items.stem:
During a school sports day, Sneha tosses a cricket ball vertically upward with a speed of 19.6 m s⁻¹ and catches it at the same height. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻² and upward as positive.
(i) What is the velocity of the ball at the highest point? (ii) Find the maximum height. (iii) Find the total time in the air. (iv) What is the acceleration of the ball at the highest point?

Assertion (A): The stopping distance of a car is proportional to the square of its initial speed.
Reason (R): For uniform retardation, v₀² = 2ax.

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: Two cars move on a straight highway in the same direction at 90 km h⁻¹ and 80 km h⁻¹. What is the magnitude of the velocity of one relative to the other?
items.markingKey: Same direction: |v₁ − v₂| = 10.0 km h⁻¹.

items.stem: Which of the following defines displacement?
items.markingKey: (b) displacement: change in position, x₂ − x₁.
options: limit of Δx/Δt as Δt → 0
change in position, x₂ − x₁
displacement ÷ time interval
total path length ÷ total time interval

items.stem: A balloon is rising vertically at a steady 10 m s⁻¹. When it is 60 m above the ground, a packet is released from it. Find the time taken by the packet to reach the ground and its speed on hitting the ground. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
items.markingKey: The packet starts with the balloon's velocity 10 m s⁻¹ upward (1). −60 = 10t − 4.9t² ⇒ t = 4.67 s (2). v² = u² + 2gh ⇒ v = 35.7 m s⁻¹ (1).

items.stem: A stone is dropped from a water tank 122.5 m high. Find the time taken to reach the ground and the speed on reaching it. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²; neglect air resistance)

Assertion (A): The slope of a position-time graph gives velocity.
Reason (R): Velocity is the rate of change of position with time.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: Rohan walks 500 m due east to a market in 5 min and then 200 m due west in 9 min. Find (i) the path length, (ii) the displacement, (iii) the average speed and (iv) the average velocity, in SI units.
items.answer: (i) 700 m (ii) 300 m east (iii) 0.833 m s⁻¹ (iv) 0.357 m s⁻¹ east
items.markingKey: Path 500 + 200 = 700 m; displacement 500 − 200 = 300 m east; time 14 min = 840 s; average speed 700/840 = 0.833 m s⁻¹; average velocity 300/840 = 0.357 m s⁻¹ east.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The velocity-time graph of a freely falling body has zero slope.
Reason (R): The acceleration of a freely falling body is constant.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false (slope = g); R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Ishita's car waits at a traffic signal. As the light turns green, it starts with uniform acceleration 4 m s⁻². At that instant Tara's car passes it at a constant 15 m s⁻¹. When and where does Ishita overtake Tara? What is Ishita's speed then?
items.answer: After 7.50 s, 113 m from the signal; speed 30.0 m s⁻¹
items.markingKey: ½at² = vt ⇒ t = 2v/a = 7.50 s (1.5); distance vt = 113 m (1); speed at = 30.0 m s⁻¹ (0.5).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about motion in a straight line is correct?
items.answer: Displacement depends only on the initial and final positions.
items.markingKey: (b) Correct: "Displacement depends only on the initial and final positions." The other three are false.
options: A body moving at constant speed must have constant velocity even if it reverses direction.
Displacement depends only on the initial and final positions.
Instantaneous speed can be different from the magnitude of instantaneous velocity.
Displacement is a scalar quantity.

items.stem: Two trains of lengths 100 m and 180 m run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 54 km h⁻¹ and 72 km h⁻¹. How long do they take to cross each other?
items.markingKey: Relative speed = 35 m s⁻¹; distance to cover = 100 + 180 = 280 m; t = 280/35 = 8.00 s.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A body can have zero velocity and still be accelerating.
Reason (R): Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, not velocity itself.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A (e.g. top of flight).
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: A scooter moving at 2 m s⁻¹ accelerates uniformly at 3 m s⁻² for 5 s. Find its final velocity and the distance travelled in this time.
items.markingKey: v = u + at = 2 + 3 × 5 = 17 m s⁻¹; s = ut + ½at² = 47.5 m.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about a ball thrown vertically upward (air resistance neglected) is correct?

items.stem: A police jeep is chasing a speeding car on a straight highway. The car moves at 72 km h⁻¹ and the jeep at 108 km h⁻¹; initially the jeep is 400 m behind. How long does the jeep take to catch the car, and how far does the car travel in that time?
Using the velocity-time graph, derive x = v₀t + ½at² for uniformly accelerated motion.
items.markingKey: Area under v-t graph = displacement (1); rectangle v₀t (1) + triangle ½(v − v₀)t (1); use v − v₀ = at (2).

items.stem: A scooter moving at 12 m s⁻¹ accelerates uniformly at 3 m s⁻² for 10 s. Find its final velocity and the distance travelled in this time.
items.markingKey: v = u + at = 12 + 3 × 10 = 42 m s⁻¹; s = ut + ½at² = 270 m.

items.stem: A uniformly accelerated body covers 16.5 m in the first 3 s and 25.5 m in the next 3 s. Find its initial velocity and acceleration.
items.answer: u = 4 m s⁻¹, a = 1 m s⁻²
items.markingKey: 16.5 = 3u + ½a(3)²; 42 = 6u + ½a(6)² (2 marks). Solving: a = (s₂ − s₁)/t² = 1 m s⁻², u = 4 m s⁻¹ (3 marks).

items.stem: Can the average speed of a body be greater than the magnitude of its average velocity? Give an example.
items.answer: Yes: when it changes direction, e.g. going to a shop and returning gives zero average velocity but non-zero average speed.
items.markingKey: Yes with reason (1 mark), example (1 mark).

items.stem: Two cars move on a straight highway towards each other at 54 km h⁻¹ and 90 km h⁻¹. What is the magnitude of the velocity of one relative to the other?
items.markingKey: Opposite directions: v₁ + v₂ = 144 km h⁻¹.

items.stem: Which of the following defines instantaneous velocity?
items.markingKey: (b) instantaneous velocity: limit of Δx/Δt as Δt → 0.
options: displacement ÷ time interval
limit of Δx/Δt as Δt → 0
total length of the path actually travelled
total path length ÷ total time interval

items.stem: A balloon is rising vertically at a steady 15 m s⁻¹. When it is 100 m above the ground, a packet is released from it. Find the time taken by the packet to reach the ground and its speed on hitting the ground. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
items.markingKey: The packet starts with the balloon's velocity 15 m s⁻¹ upward (1). −100 = 15t − 4.9t² ⇒ t = 6.30 s (2). v² = u² + 2gh ⇒ v = 46.7 m s⁻¹ (1).

items.stem: Rahul walks 450 m due east to a market in 10 min and then 150 m due west in 5 min. Find (i) the path length, (ii) the displacement, (iii) the average speed and (iv) the average velocity, in SI units.
items.answer: (i) 600 m (ii) 300 m east (iii) 0.667 m s⁻¹ (iv) 0.333 m s⁻¹ east
items.markingKey: Path 450 + 150 = 600 m; displacement 450 − 150 = 300 m east; time 15 min = 900 s; average speed 600/900 = 0.667 m s⁻¹; average velocity 300/900 = 0.333 m s⁻¹ east.

items.stem: Rohan's car waits at a traffic signal. As the light turns green, it starts with uniform acceleration 2.5 m s⁻². At that instant Dev's car passes it at a constant 15 m s⁻¹. When and where does Rohan overtake Dev? What is Rohan's speed then?
items.answer: After 12.0 s, 180 m from the signal; speed 30.0 m s⁻¹
items.markingKey: ½at² = vt ⇒ t = 2v/a = 12.0 s (1.5); distance vt = 180 m (1); speed at = 30.0 m s⁻¹ (0.5).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about motion in a straight line is correct?
items.answer: Average speed is never less than the magnitude of average velocity over the same interval.
items.markingKey: (c) Correct: "Average speed is never less than the magnitude of average velocity over the same interval." The other three are false.
options: Instantaneous speed can be different from the magnitude of instantaneous velocity.
Average speed always equals the magnitude of average velocity.
Average speed is never less than the magnitude of average velocity over the same interval.
A body moving at constant speed must have constant velocity even if it reverses direction.

items.stem: Two trains of lengths 100 m and 180 m run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 72 km h⁻¹ and 45 km h⁻¹. How long do they take to cross each other?
items.markingKey: Relative speed = 32.5 m s⁻¹; distance to cover = 100 + 180 = 280 m; t = 280/32.5 = 8.62 s.

items.stem: A police jeep is chasing a speeding car on a straight highway. The car moves at 54 km h⁻¹ and the jeep at 72 km h⁻¹; initially the jeep is 1000 m behind. How long does the jeep take to catch the car, and how far does the car travel in that time?
items.markingKey: Relative speed (72 − 54) km h⁻¹ = 5 m s⁻¹ (1); t = 1000/5 = 200 s (1); car moves 15 × 200 = 3000 m (1).
